read.title: How to Give Feedback That Helps
read.text:
Good feedback is specific, timely, and focused on behavior rather than personality. Instead of saying "Your report was bad," say "The report needs a clearer summary on the first page." This tells the person exactly what to change.

Timing matters, too. Feedback given a week later loses much of its value, because people may not remember the details. Try to share your thoughts within a day or two.

Finally, make it a conversation. Ask the other person how they felt about their work, and agree together on one or two next steps.
